Create ONE original standalone Kalistar character illustration, not a card. Vertical 4:5 composition for a 737 x 921 artwork window. Mandatory visual identity: detailed narrative fantasy PAINTING, visibly angular broken brushstrokes and tactile color planes across every material, expressive painted anatomy, worn cloth/leather/metal, crisp focal face and main gesture with progressively softer edges away from them. Match the hand-painted, weathered yet beautiful identity of Kalistar's Momo and Valazar, not photography, photorealism, smooth CGI, anime, cartoon or generic concept-art airbrushing. Do not add uniform digital noise. Advanced post-apocalyptic fantasy world: clothing stays characterful, practical, crafted and layered; subtle inventive technology belongs mostly to tools, weapons and small mounted Kalistel crystals. Do not turn everyone into a medieval knight or a sci-fi soldier. Background MUST be restrained: two or three large environmental shapes and atmospheric space, no busy city, piles of props, ornate wall fill or endless particles. One adult character only. Credible weight, grips, joints and object contact; normally one head, two arms and two legs. Essential face/hands central with breathing room for later card cropping. No text, logos, flags, frame, numbers or interface. Tell a specific emotional moment rather than a mannequin pose. 
SUBJECT AND MOMENT: An older male Okami, an organically integrated permanent human-wolf hybrid: charcoal and silver fur across head, neck and exposed forearms, intelligent amber eyes, one subtly bent ear, expressive brows and muzzle, dexterous furred humanlike hands. Black and deep FOREST GREEN wool coat, small silver closures, no red uniform. He stands sideways leaning into wind and carefully strikes a compact hanging three-plate storm chime with a short magnetically tuned mallet. One hand steadies the frame, the other holds the mallet properly; the metal instrument is bolted to a waist-high mountain-post, not floating. He listens with one ear turned and eyes almost closed, recognizing the safe crossing from its clear tone. A tiny cold-white seam along the mallet, restrained technical artifact. Three-quarter figure, low viewpoint, large quiet snowy mountain plane and cloud behind; warm late sunlight on muzzle and green collar. His posture, fur shoulders and asymmetric coat opening visibly belong to this wolf-human body, not an animal head pasted onto a generic man.
